title: Guardrails: async eval runner (queue + worker), retry/timeout policy, and persisted results
author: Olivia Grant
release_notes: Internal: adds Guardrails async eval runner (job queue + worker) used by Optimize gating. No customer-facing changes; gated behind feature flags.
body: Summary: This PR introduces the Guardrails async eval runner used by Optimize “apply” gating. It adds (1) a persistent job queue, (2) a worker process to execute eval-harness runs out-of-band, (3) a consistent timeout/retry policy, and (4) a result persistence model that upstream services can query for a stable decision artifact. Motivation: We need gating checks to be reliable and audit-friendly, but running eval suites inline in the Optimize apply request path is too slow and creates cascading failure modes when eval infra is degraded. This runner decouples apply UX/API from eval execution while preserving deterministic inputs/outputs and providing a single place to implement retries, backoff, and timeouts. Scope: This PR does not change Optimize apply behavior by default; callers can enqueue jobs via an internal API when the guardrails feature flag is enabled. Design: Queue + persistence are Postgres-backed (control-plane DB) so we have an auditable record and don’t lose jobs on deploys. Workers acquire a lease on jobs using a compare-and-set update (lease_expires_at + worker_id) to avoid duplicate execution. Results are written as a summary record plus pointers to artifacts stored in object storage. Core primitives: (a) GuardrailsEvalJob: job_id (UUID), tenant_id, route_id, model_id/model_version, prompt_set_rev, suite_id(s), config_delta_hash, requested_by (actor), created_at, state (QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/TIMED_OUT/CANCELED), priority, not_before, attempt_count, max_attempts, last_error_code, last_error_message (redacted), and audit_context JSON (stored but size-limited + PII-safe). (b) GuardrailsEvalAttempt: attempt_id, job_id, started_at, finished_at, runner_version, worker_id, timeout_applied_ms, exit_status, error_code. (c) GuardrailsEvalResult: job_id, aggregated_metrics_json (schema validated), ci_json (optional), sample_size, gating_mode_metadata (prompt_set_rev, suite rev, harness commit), artifacts (s3://… pointers), and result_checksum for integrity. Timeout/retry policy: Per-attempt hard timeout (default 25m; configurable per suite class) enforced at the worker level; jobs that exceed are marked TIMED_OUT and retried up to max_attempts (default 2) with exponential backoff + jitter. We treat the following as retryable: harness transient failures, worker preemption, object store timeouts, and known “flake” grader timeouts. We do NOT retry: schema validation failures, invalid inputs (missing model version, invalid prompt-set rev), or explicit “suite not supported” errors. Concurrency/limits: Worker is configured with (1) global concurrency, (2) per-tenant concurrency, and (3) per-suite class concurrency to avoid a single tenant or a heavy suite starving others. We also add a queue depth guardrail to shed new jobs (429 with retry-after) when backlog exceeds a configured threshold; this is not enabled by default but is wired. API: Added internal service endpoints under /internal/guardrails/eval-jobs: POST create job (idempotency key supported), GET job status + result summary, POST cancel job (best-effort). Responses include stable job_id for audit linking. All endpoints require service-to-service auth and are restricted to the Optimize/Control Plane callers (RBAC for internal services via existing policy bundles). Observability: Emits structured logs per job lifecycle transition and adds metrics: guardrails_eval_jobs_enqueued_total, guardrails_eval_jobs_running, guardrails_eval_job_latency_ms (enqueue->terminal), guardrails_eval_attempts_total by exit_status, guardrails_eval_queue_backlog, and guardrails_eval_worker_lease_conflicts_total. Metrics include bounded labels: suite_class, result_state, error_code; tenant_id is intentionally excluded to avoid cardinality blowups (see notes + review feedback). Data retention: Job + result summaries retained for 30 days (configurable; aligns with current audit requirements draft). Artifact pointers are stored, but artifact lifecycle is handled by existing bucket policies; this PR does not change object storage retention. Safety/PII: Inputs (prompt sets) are referenced by revision id only; raw prompts are not stored in the runner DB. Error messages are redacted via the shared redaction helper (max 2KB; strips likely secrets). Testing: Added unit tests for state transitions, leasing behavior, retry classification, and timeout handling. Added an integration test that spins a fake harness binary that sleeps/returns a payload to validate timeouts + result persistence. Rollout: Behind feature flag guardrails.evalRunner.enabled (default false). When enabled, callers may enqueue jobs; no behavior change is wired in this PR. Follow-ups: (1) Cache identical eval runs keyed by (model_version, prompt_set_rev, suite, config_delta) (tracked in ENG-3916 / PR TBD). (2) Integrate with Optimize apply endpoint to switch from inline to async flow with proper UI states (ENG-3913/ENG-3917). (3) Add admin tooling for replay/inspection (ENG-? later PR).
commits: guardrails/runner: add eval_jobs + eval_job_attempts + eval_results tables and repository layer
guardrails/runner: implement job leasing + state machine (queued->running->terminal)
guardrails/runner: add worker loop w/ concurrency limits and per-attempt timeouts
guardrails/runner: integrate eval-harness invocation wrapper + artifact upload helper
guardrails/api: add internal endpoints for enqueue/status/cancel
obs: add metrics + structured logging + redaction on error payloads
tests: unit + integration coverage for retries/timeouts/leases
conversation: Jordan Lee (review): Can we document the job state machine and make transitions explicit? I’m worried about callers seeing inconsistent states (e.g., FAILED but with partial result).

Olivia Grant (author): Added an explicit transition table in code comments + tests. Also ensured result rows are only written in SUCCEEDED (or FAILED w/ schema-valid error summary but no metrics payload).
Sean Gallagher (review): Backoff values feel aggressive. If the runner is degraded we’ll just pile on. Can we cap retries and add jitter?
Olivia Grant (author): Updated retry policy: max_attempts default 2, backoff base 30s with jitter and max 10m. Also added a metric for backlog and lease conflicts so we can alert before cascading.
Logan Wright (review): Please avoid tenant_id as a metric label; cardinality is going to explode. We can correlate via logs + job_id.
Olivia Grant (author): Removed tenant_id labels. Added suite_class + error_code only. job_id is included in structured logs for correlation.
Ethan Park (review): How do we ensure idempotency when Optimize retries enqueue? We need stable linking for audit events.
Olivia Grant (author): Added idempotency_key support on POST create. We upsert on (tenant_id, idempotency_key) and return the original job_id if already created.
Chloe Martin (review): API response shape should be stable for console; can we include a minimal “result_summary” even when running?
Olivia Grant (author): Added result_summary field (empty until terminal) and standardized timestamps + state enum.
Jordan Lee (follow-up): Lease acquisition uses lease_expires_at; what happens if worker dies mid-run?
Olivia Grant (author): Lease expires and another worker can pick it up; attempts are tracked. Harness invocation is wrapped so we don’t double-upload artifacts; artifact path includes attempt_id.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Good with this as long as feature flag remains default-off and we add alerting in the follow-up dashboards PR.
Ethan Park (approval): LGTM. Please link this PR in the ENG-3914 ticket and note that apply endpoint integration will follow.
Olivia Grant (author): Done. Linked in ENG-3914 and added follow-ups in description.
